Hypothesis of the change: The parent's criticality penalty in the area-balance repair uses `max(1.0, area)` which over-weights large macros and can over-constrain balance; replacing it with a normalized, area-independent criticality penalty (crit * mean_area) keeps the criticality preference but reduces the risk of failing to reach the area target, improving robustness while retaining the proven co-location benefit.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.512 robust(mean-std)=+0.141 min_case=+0.135 all_valid=True

  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.135 dWNS=+8.4% dTNS=+17.1% overflow~138
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: all runs valid, robust score +0.141, no case regressed. Gains concentrate in WNS/TNS (ariane133 +15.6%/+23.9%, bp +17.7%/+16.8%, bp_fe +8.4%/+17.1%) with overflow ~126–138, consistent with the normalized penalty relaxing over-constraint on large macros while preserving co-location. Next step: sweep the mean_area scaling factor (e.g., 0.5×–2×) across more seeds to confirm the balance-vs-criticality tradeoff is stable and not seed-specific.
